feedback: Written before this candidate races. Evidence from iteration 1 (±0.03 m array, 13/20 oval finishes, 1/20 s-bend, 0/20 slalom, max_error 0.062 to 0.063 m on the sharp tracks, 1.1 to 1.3 line-loss events per run) shows that the failures are off-track exits on bends, not speed limits, since the oval finishes in 1.83 s. The Integrator kept your span-only change and the iteration 1 controller unchanged, so the next race isolates the wider span. Decision rules for the next race: if s-bend and slalom off-track counts fall and max_error drops below about 0.05 m, keep ±0.04 m and then test whether a larger weight shape is needed. If the sharp tracks still exit with max_error above 0.05 m and line-loss events of 1 or more, change sensor_size to 0.016 m at the same spacing to close dead zones between sensors. If oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.2 while max_error is low, that is a weight problem, so reduce the controller weights rather than changing geometry. If the robot completes with completion_time above about 3 s, raise wheel_radius to 0.035 m.
requested_changes: If s-bend or slalom still exit with max_error above 0.05 m after the ±0.04 m span, try sensor_size 0.016 m at the same 0.02 m spacing, because iteration 1 showed line-loss events of 1.1 to 1.3 per run on sharp bends, which suggests gaps between sensors.

If the wider span lowers off-track exits but the oval still shows steering_oscillation above 0.2, keep this geometry and let the Integrator scale weights, since iteration 1 oval oscillation was 0.31 with max_error 0.044, which is not an error-driven problem.
Raise wheel_radius to 0.035 m only if a future race completes with completion_time above about 3 s, because iteration 1 oval finished in 1.83 s, so speed was not the limit.
